J&K DGP reviews ongoing anti-terror operations in Poonch
results.description: Jammu, Sep 14 (IANS) J&K Director General of Police (DGP), Nalin Prabhat, reviewed the ongoing anti-terror operations in Poonch district on Monday, officials said. The DGP, who was accompanied by Inspector General of Police (IGP) Jammu Zone, Tejinder Singh, held a detailed review of the operations currently underway in the district, as well as its overall security situation. "The DGP was briefed about the latest developments, operational preparedness and coordination among different security agencies on the ground. The visit assumes significance in view of recent attempts at infiltration and movement of Pakistan-based Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT) terrorists in the Pir Panjal region," an official said. Recently, the State Investigation Agency (SIA) conducted multiple raids in the Mandi and Surankote areas of Poonch (as well as Udhampur) targeting networks propagating radicalisation and cross-border communication. The SIA recovered evidence indicating that several locals were in direct communication with handlers across the Line of Control (LoC). These channels were allegedly utilised to spread secessionist narratives and advance online radicalisation. In early September, border troops detected a group of terrorists attempting to cross the LoC near Dabbi village in the Balakote sector (Mendhar). A heavy exchange of fire ensued, leading to extensive combing operations in the local forest belts. Massive cordon-and-search operations (CASO) remain active in remote forest pockets including Dhara Sangla, Bhatadurian, and Kherowali Dhok. These were triggered by technical intelligence and local observations of suspicious movements near critical infrastructure projects like the under-construction Pir Panjal tunnel. High-level security assessments and intelligence-based raids dictate the current anti-terror operational landscape in the Poonch district. Joint security grids involving the Indian Army, Jammu and Kashmir Police, and specialised central agencies have escalated measures to thwart cross-border infiltration and dismantle terror networks. --IANS sq/vd

results.title: Bhupender Yadav reviews Great Indian Bustard conservation work in Gujarat’s Kachchh
results.description: Kachchh/New Delhi, Sep 14 (IANS) Environment Minister Bhupender Yadav on Monday reviewed conservation and habitat-management efforts of the Gujarat Forest Department and the Wildlife Institute of India at the Great Indian Bustard (GIB) habitat at Naliya in the Kachchh district. In a message on X, Yadav said, “During my visit to the Great Indian Bustard Habitat in Naliya, Kutch, I interacted with representatives of the Jat Sumra and Darbar communities in 'Khatala Sabha' to garner their support in the conservation efforts of the Great Indian Bustard.” “Under the leadership of PM Shri @narendramodi ji, India has been laying emphasis on community-led stewardship for environmental protection and species conservation. The local pastoralist and agricultural groups in Kutch are key to ensuring the success of GIB conservation,” he said. The minister also inaugurated the Soft Release Centre for the Great Indian Bustard at the facility and interacted with officials, said an official statement. He was briefed on the significant on-ground progress achieved in the GIB landscape. It included restoration of around 11 sq. km. of grassland infested with the invasive Prosopis juliflora; raising of 30 km of predator-proof fencing covering 15 sq. km; the pioneering 'jump-start' intervention in which infertile eggs laid by wild GIB females were replaced with viable eggs from the conservation breeding programme. Yadav was informed that the resulting chick from the second such attempt has survived beyond the critical first three months in the wild – a landmark result for the species' recovery in Gujarat. He also flagged off 33 new patrolling and rescue vehicles for forest and wildlife conservation efforts. These vehicles would be utilised across various divisions under the Kachchh Forest Circle for forest protection, forest development, wildlife protection, field patrolling, monitoring and quick-response activities. The Minister later visited the Hariyalu Gram plantation in Sayara and was briefed on the Sayara Van Kavach initiative and an associated bee-keeping unit. He planted a sapling at the site, inaugurated the Sayara Van Kavach and witnessed the exchange of a Memorandum of Understanding with the Deendayal Port Authority for plantation activities. --IANS rch/uk

results.title: NHAI to upgrade 1033 National Highway helpline with AI, real-time location tracking
results.description: New Delhi, Sep 14 (IANS) The National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) on Monday said it is planning to upgrade its existing 1033 National Highway Helpline with advanced technology to provide faster and better assistance to travellers. According to the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways, the upgraded 1033 helpline will use technologies such as artificial intelligence (AI), real-time location tracking and smart emergency-response systems. “These improvements will help the 1033 National Highway helpline identify the location of callers, understand calls in different Indian languages and send the right assistance to the location more quickly. Human operators will continue to play an important role, especially in emergencies where human judgement and decision-making are essential,” the NHAI said in a statement. The Indian Highways Management Company Limited (IHMCL), a company promoted by NHAI, has invited an Expression of Interest (EOI) from companies and consortia for the development, design, deployment, operation and maintenance of the next-generation 1033 helpline and call centre. IHMCL will seek suggestions and technical inputs from industry experts to develop a reliable, scalable and future-ready system. Relevant industry best practices will also be considered while finalising the requirements. The upgraded 1033 helpline is expected to make assistance on National Highways faster, more coordinated and more convenient for citizens. By combining technology with human support, NHAI aims to further improve the safety and travel experience of highway users across the country. It is aimed at providing better systems for receiving calls and sending help to the required location; real-time capture of the caller’s location to help emergency teams reach the spot; AI-assisted handling of calls in different Indian languages; and Intelligent systems to help identify and send the most suitable ambulance, crane or patrol vehicle. It will also help in timely advisories to highway users about incidents and other important developments and provide improved coordination between the helpline, emergency services and National Highway operations teams. --IANS na/
